answer: A stake-weighted reputation system resists Sybil attacks by making each new identity post a refundable bond that grows with its transaction history, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive. Honest agents accumulate verifiable work records that peers echo as endorsements, while a caught cheater's identities collapse together: the shared bond is slashed and its reputation falls into a downward spiral. The network becomes a narrow canyon, cheap to enter honestly but costly to flood with sock puppets, since every duplicate identity must pay its own way in.
